messages:
opsbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: sudden latency/throughput regression in runtime after the 2026-03-15 deploy (deploy id d-7f3c). Alerts firing: p95 latency > 850ms for generation endpoints, throughput down ~30%

pagerduty: paging sanjay (oncall) -> alert: runtime-high-p95

sanjay (oncall): On it. grabbing context. Which model/route is the spike on?

emma (release): looks concentrated on hosted/gpt-redwood-v1 and a subset of heavy prompt routes. Canary rollout of batching changes (runtime_batching_v2) went to 20% two hours ago. deploy-bot shows rollout is still progressing.

liang: logs show lots of kernel fallbacks on the new quantized path:
```
[2026-03-15T17:42:12Z] kernel_selector: requested cuda_fp16_optim; fallback to avx2_generic due to missing kernel for seq_len>1024
[2026-03-15T17:42:13Z] batching: rejected batch (size 128) -> falling back to single-request path
```

maria-sre: that fallback would explain throughput drop and p95 increase. Are we seeing increased GPU SM utilization or CPU stealing?

liang: GPU utilization is lower than expected; CPU sys is high on the runtime hosts running fallback code paths. Batching queue depth is low because kernel rejects batches.

emma (release): @sanjay we should stop the rollout and flip the kill-switch for runtime_batching_v2. Can someone toggle flags and pause the deploy?

sanjay (oncall): Acknowledged. Pausing rollout now. Handoff to emma to run feature flag kill.

emma (release): Hitting the FF console -> toggling runtime_batching_v2 -> set state=off for hosted cluster. API call:
```
curl -X POST "https://ff.redwood.internal/api/v1/toggles/runtime_batching_v2/off" -H "Authorization: Bearer ***"
```

opsbot: feature-flag updated: runtime_batching_v2 -> OFF for env=hosted (user: emma). :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy d-7f3c: rollout paused at 20% (triggered by flag change).

liang: after kill-switch, observed kernel selector back to stable kernels and batching re-enabled. preliminary p95 back to ~210ms within 4 minutes.

alex-ux: any customer-facing incidents? I haven't seen support tickets yet.

maria-sre: Alert matrix: ~12k affected requests in last 30m, error rate up 0.4% (mainly timeouts 504). Top impacted tenants: acme-inc (dedicated?), beta-platform (hosted). Reached out to Support.

sanjay (oncall): Good mitigation. Next step: decide rollback vs partial revert to fix kernel selector incompat. Is there a quick patch?

liang: Root cause: batching path requested a specialized CUDA kernel variant that isn't available for the new quantized artifact for sequence lengths above 1024. Two short-term options:
- revert grouping: rollback binary to previous runtime (d-7f2b) across hosted (safest)
- patch selector: force kernel selector to prefer generic CUDA kernel even if less optimized (requires patch & quick canary)

emma (release): I prefer rollback to minimize customer risk. Can we do a coordinated rollback of the served artifact to d-7f2b for hosted?

deploy-bot: rollback command queued. Confirming: rollback to d-7f2b for cluster=hosted? (yes/no)

sanjay (oncall): yes, confirm rollback. Also will contact sales/CS for any high-touch customers.

emma (release): Rolling back now -> running:
```
releases rollback --cluster hosted --to d-7f2b --by emma --reason "kernel fallback causing latency regression"
```

opsbot: rollback started: d-7f3c -> d-7f2b (hosted). Staged: 3 regions.

liang: monitoring logs: rollback step 1 complete in us-west1, runtime svc restarted, batches accepted, kernel binds to cuda_fp16_optim again. p95 down to 180ms in us-west1.

maria-sre: Noted customer impact window: 2026-03-15T17:40:00Z -> 2026-03-15T17:56:00Z (approx). CS will notify customers in affected list; shared status page update drafted.

alex-ux: prepping a short status blurb for status.redwood.ai: "We briefly observed increased latency for some generation requests after a deploy; mitigation applied and full rollback completed. Investigating root cause."

maria-sre: CS update: reached out to acme-inc and beta-platform, provided timeline and apology. No SLA credit asked yet.

sanjay (oncall): handing off to maria-sre for postmortem and to liang+release for fix. I'm going offline in 10m but will stay reachable for escalation.

liang: immediate action items:
- revert batching selector change in next stable patch and add unit test for kernel availability matrix
- add runtime health check to detect kernel fallback and auto-suppress rollout if fallback detected
- expand canary from static 20% to a canary that validates kernel availability before increasing weight

emma (release): noted. I'll create the release revert PR and coordinate with QA for a fast patch. Estimated remediation PR + canary patch within 4 hours.

maria-sre: creating incident ticket INC-2026-0315-runtime-regression, assigning owners: liang (engineer), emma (release), maria-sre (postmortem), sanjay (oncall). Will run 1h postmortem meeting at 09:00 tomorrow.

opsbot: incident created INC-2026-0315-runtime-regression (link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0315-runtime-regression).

alex-ux: any followups for UX docs or changelog? We should mention the batching behavior caveat in the runtime release notes.

liang: will add to the changelog and add a preflight check in the compile pipeline to ensure kernels exist for the target quantized artifact.

sanjay (oncall): closing the immediate on-call loop: mitigation successful, rollback complete. If anything regresses ping the SRE channel and re-pager. Good job team. :clap:

maria-sre: collecting artifacts: logs, timeline, feature-flag state, rollout history, kernel-selector traces. I'll attach to the incident.

emma (release): thanks all. I'll follow up with the PR link and ETA in the incident ticket.

deploy-bot: rollback completed across all regions (d-7f3c -> d-7f2b). All services reporting nominal.

opsbot: SUMMARY: cause=kernel-compatibility mismatch after batching/quantization change; impact=latency spike & throughput drop for hosted generation routes; mitigation=feature-flag kill + rollback; next=patch & preflight.

maria-sre: postmortem outline posted to INC-2026-0315-runtime-regression. Meeting invite sent.

sanjay (oncall): offcall. Good job.

alex-ux: +1 to a clearer staging -> prod kernel compatibility gate.

emma (release): will follow up in ticket with concrete timelines.

(THREAD END)
